inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares Q2 2026 10-Q (307.6M). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and RSG's buybacks (TTM $1.47B) more than fund the flat count -- they shrink it, which this model treats as value-neutral capital return rather than per-share accretion.
inputs.sbc_source: XBRL ShareBasedCompensation: FY2024 $42M, 9M-2025 $33M; tag absent for Q4-25 and 2026, so TTM Jun-26 estimated at $45M on the FY24/9M-25 run-rate, plus ~$15M est. tax withheld on net-share settlement (not tagged; Q1-26 StockIssuedDuringPeriodValueNewIssues -$14M is the withholding signature). Immaterial at ~0.36% of revenue either way.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Rf 4.3% (10y UST), beta ~0.75 (defensive waste oligopoly), ERP 5.0% -> CoE ~8.0%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.6% (interest $574M FY25 on ~$13.5B avg debt), after-tax ~3.6%; D/V ~18% at market -> ~7.2%. Rounded up to 7.5% for leverage creep from debt-funded M&A and PFAS liability uncertainty. Same WACC in all three scenarios (risk charged once, via scenario paths and weights).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease cost (~$60M/yr, $226M liability) sits inside EBITDA as rent, so operating leases are NOT in net debt; finance leases ($293M) are inside total_debt (LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations) and their principal is therefore NOT deducted from flows. One treatment each, never both.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI immaterial ($1M on the June-2026 balance sheet); no adjustment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (dcf-methods routing: US operating company -- a collection/transfer/landfill/recycling operator whose value is a free-cash-flow stream; not a REIT, bank, holdco or LIC). Adaptations file not needed (USD filer, USD quote, US GAAP leases, no NCI, SBC non-zero). FY0 is TTM to Jun-2026 so that year 1 (Jul-26..Jun-27) does not re-count H1-2026 cash already in the June balance sheet. REVENUE BASIS: uses us-gaap RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax (FY25 $16,591M, the reported net revenue that guidance is framed on); the Metrics.csv Revenue column carries the XBRL `Revenues` tag (FY25 $19,027M), which is GROSS of intercompany eliminations and overstates revenue ~15% -- every margin computed off that column is ~4pp too low. TTM components: net revenue 16,891; GAAP EBITDA (OI + D&A) 5,234 (31.0%); D&A 1,866 (11.0%); capex 1,889 (11.2%); OCF 4,542; asset-sale proceeds 12; reported FCF = OCF - capex + proceeds = 2,665 (levered, after ~$500M cash interest). Owner FCF (last_fcf) = 2,665 - 60 = 2,605. The engine's flows are UNLEVERED (EBIT x (1-t) + D&A - capex), so year-1 owner FCF (~$2.9B) sits above the levered TTM figure by roughly the after-tax interest bill; that is consistent, not a jump. EBITDA margin path is ex-SBC and NET of ~0.9pp of cash spent on landfill capping/closure/post-closure and environmental remediation (ARO settlements $70M FY25 plus remediation) that adjusted EBITDA excludes but OCF pays; the $2.8B of accrued closure/environmental liabilities is therefore charged in the flows and NOT put in the equity bridge. ACQUISITIONS: growth paths are ORGANIC (price minus volume) from year 2; tuck-in M&A ($1.43B FY25, $865M H1-26) is treated as NPV-neutral capital deployment, so neither the acquired revenue nor the spend is modelled. Deals closed by June 2026 are in net debt, and their rollover revenue is in year 1. Buybacks: active repurchaser ($870M FY25, $659M H1-26), so the flat count is funded with real cash. CASH TAX: FY25 cash taxes $206M (~8% of pre-tax) and H1-26 $79M are depressed by 100% bonus depreciation (deferred tax +$269M FY25) and purchased solar/renewable tax credits; book ETR ~17.5%. Modelled 15% ramping to 22% by year 8 -- not perpetuating the shelter, but not snapping to statutory either since bonus depreciation on a growing capex base defers tax persistently.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (7.1%) is >30% below EPS 5yr CAGR (17.7%): EPS is lifted by buybacks (~3% of shares retired since FY2020), margin expansion and the FY2020 COVID trough base. Revenue CAGRs (7.1% 3yr / 10.3% 5yr, net-revenue basis) include the US Ecology acquisition (2022) and ~$1B/yr of tuck-ins; organic growth is ~4-5% (core price 5-6%, volume -1%). The DCF uses organic growth, not the selected equity CAGR, because M&A spend is not modelled.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs FY2022->FY2025 (3yr) and FY2020->FY2025 (5yr). Revenue from RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax (net), not the CSV's gross `Revenues` column. Owner FCF = OCF - capex - SBC (FY25 SBC estimated $44M on the 9M run-rate). SBC is flat at ~$40M while FCF grew, so the owner-FCF CAGR is marginally ABOVE the reported one -- no hidden stock-comp funding of growth.

base.narrative: Core price runs 4-5% (CPI-linked municipal escalators plus open-market pricing in an oligopoly), volume flat to -1% as construction/industrial recovers slowly; EBITDA margin creeps ~0.7pp over five years from pricing over cost, route automation and Polymer Center contribution, then flat. Capex stays a touch above D&A for landfill cell build and fleet.

bull.narrative: Volume turns positive as housing/industrial activity recovers while core price holds 5%+; Blue Polymers and the Environmental Solutions (US Ecology, Shamrock) platform grow above the core and lift mix; route optimisation, automated side-loaders and fleet electrification take EBITDA margin to ~33%. Bonus depreciation keeps cash tax low for longer.

bear.narrative: Pricing power fades to ~CPI as disinflation resets escalators and WM/WCN/GFL compete harder for municipal bids; volume stays negative. EPA's PFAS hazardous-substance designation forces leachate treatment and higher closure/post-closure spend (capex and cash closure costs up), driver wage inflation compresses EBITDA margin ~1.3pp, and bonus-depreciation deferral unwinds toward a full cash tax rate.

scenario_narratives.base: Republic compounds as a price-led oligopolist: 4-5% core price offsets -1% volume, organic revenue ~4-4.5% decaying to 3%, margins inch up 0.7pp on automation and the Polymer Centers, capex stays slightly above D&A. Tuck-in M&A continues but is assumed to earn its cost of capital, so it adds nothing to value here.
scenario_narratives.bull: Volume recovers alongside sticky 5%+ pricing; Environmental Solutions and Blue Polymers (food-grade rPET/HDPE with Ravago) grow faster than the core and command premium pricing from brand-owner recycled-content mandates; automation and EV fleet take EBITDA margin to ~33%. Organic growth 5-5.5% for four years.
scenario_narratives.bear: The pricing tailwind fades with inflation, municipal re-bids get competitive, PFAS regulation (leachate treatment, Superfund designation) and labour inflation take ~1.3pp off margin and push capex up, and cash taxes normalise as bonus-depreciation deferral unwinds. Organic growth settles at 2.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20%: no solvency or refinancing risk (investment-grade, ~2.7x levered, laddered maturities) but PFAS is a live, industry-wide regulatory cost whose size is unknown. Base 55%: the business is unusually predictable -- contracted, CPI-escalated, non-discretionary -- so the central path deserves more weight than the house 50%. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): the bull needs volume recovery AND margin expansion AND above-core growth in Polymers/Environmental Solutions at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A wide-moat, low-variance compounder priced as one. The owner-FCF DCF on organic growth and a 20x terminal cap values the equity below the market, which pays ~27x EV/unlevered owner FCF -- i.e. the market capitalises both the moat at a lower discount rate than 7.5% and the expectation that ~$1B/yr of tuck-in M&A earns well above its cost of capital. Neither is in the house base case.
key_risks_to_valuation: PFAS: EPA hazardous-substance designation could add leachate-treatment opex and closure/post-closure cost industry-wide; not quantified in filings
Terminal cap binds in base and bear (Gordon at 7.5%/3.0% is ~22.9x); value is sensitive to the cap and to WACC
M&A excluded: if tuck-ins earn well above WACC (plausible -- RSG buys at 6-8x EBITDA and synergises), the model understates value
Cash tax: persistence of bonus depreciation and solar tax-credit purchases could keep cash tax well below the 22% terminal rate
Leverage creep: ~$14B debt and rising if M&A and buybacks continue to be debt-funded
